title: U.S. House · Ohio's 9th District
area: Northwest Ohio along Lake Erie, including Toledo and Lucas County.

context.text: Ohio's congressional map was redrawn for 2026, changing the 9th District's boundaries from those used in 2024. Analysts said the new lines favor Republicans more than the old ones did: Kaptur won by 13 points in 2022 under the old lines, while Trump carried the new district's territory by about eleven points in 2024 (an estimated 54.8%-44.2% Trump-Harris under the 2026 lines, per The Downballot). Incumbent Marcy Kaptur (D) ran unopposed in the May 5 Democratic primary. Derek Merrin (R), a former Ohio House member, won a five-way Republican primary with 44.1% of the vote. Libertarian Matthew Althaus won his primary but was later disqualified from the November ballot. Kathy McKinstry filed as an independent write-in candidate.

summary.text: Marcy Kaptur is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in Ohio's 9th Congressional District, which she has represented since 1983, making her the longest-serving woman in the history of the U.S. House. She sits on the House Appropriations Committee.

background.text: Born in Toledo, Ohio, in 1946; earned a bachelor's degree in history from the University of Wisconsin (1968) and a master's in urban planning from the University of Michigan (1974).
Worked as an urban planner for the Toledo-Lucas County Plan Commissions (1969-1975) and as director of planning at the National Center for Urban Ethnic Affairs (1975-1977).
Served as an urban policy advisor in the Carter administration (1977-1979) and was pursuing a doctorate in urban affairs at MIT when she first won election to Congress in 1982.

priorities.text: Jobs, costs and the economy: says strengthening the economy is her top priority, and that she is fighting to bring jobs back to Ohio, remove tax breaks from companies that ship jobs overseas, and secure tariffs to protect Ohio-based manufacturers.
Supports job training and technical-skills programs as an alternative path to good-paying work that doesn't require a four-year degree.
Says she has fought to protect Social Security and Medicare from cuts and privatization.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says she is fighting for tariffs to protect Ohio-based factories and companies from unfair trade agreements.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (119th Congress, 2025-2026), including the Agriculture-Rural Development-FDA, Energy and Water Development, and Defense subcommittees.
Was ranking member of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development in the 118th Congress (2023-2024) and chaired that subcommittee in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

summary.text: Derek Merrin is the Republican nominee for Ohio's 9th Congressional District. He is a former Ohio House representative from Lucas County who served eight years in the state legislature, including as elected leader of the House Republican Caucus and chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee.

background.text: Born in Smithtown, New York; earned a B.A. from the University of Toledo (2008) and a master's in public administration from Bowling Green State University (2009).
Worked as a business owner, realtor and state auditor; served as a councilman and later mayor of the city of Waterville, Ohio.
Lost the 2024 general election for this seat to Marcy Kaptur under the previous district lines, 48.3%-47.6%.

priorities.text: Says he is a strong advocate for lower taxes, simplifying the tax code, and promoting transparency, citing his role leading efforts in the Ohio legislature to cut the state income tax.
Says he advocated for policies to reduce health-care costs, promote price transparency, and expand patient access through fewer regulations as chairman of the Ohio House Health Committee.

positions.summary: His campaign website says he successfully led efforts to cut Ohio's state income tax and is a strong advocate for lower taxes.
His campaign website says he led efforts to expand school choice while in the Ohio legislature.
Voted yes on SB 215 (allowing adults 21 and older to carry a concealed handgun without a permit), which passed the Ohio House 58-36 on 2022-03-02.

stated.summary: His campaign website says he played a key role in Ohio's constitutional-carry law allowing Ohioans to carry firearms without a permit.

record.text: Voted yes on SB 215 (allowing adults 21 and older to carry a concealed handgun without a permit), which passed the Ohio House 58-36 on 2022-03-02.

As an Ohio House member, sponsored and passed HB 116 repealing the state sales tax on prescription eyewear, and HB 592 repealing the Financial Institution Tax on Small Business Investment Companies, according to his campaign.

Sponsored the Epinephrine Accessibility Act (HB 101) and the Down Syndrome Non-Discrimination Act (HB 214), and a bill simplifying the process for homeowners to challenge their property valuations (HB 118), according to his campaign.
Chaired the Ohio House Ways and Means Committee in the 134th General Assembly and previously chaired the House Health Committee.
